title: Ordeo component layout
description: Describes the composition and layout of one component and its parts. Tokens hold the styling and every measure (gap, margin, inset); this file holds what the tokens cannot: which parts exist, what they hold, how they nest, and how they are placed and laid out. It is platform neutral and is consumed by tooling that generates the platform-specific code.

$schema.description: Path or URL of this schema, so the IDE can validate the file.

components.description: Every renderable unit of this component. The first entry is the root; the rest are the parts it (or another part) references through slots. Each entry becomes one component in the generated code.

component.description: One renderable unit: the root component or one of its parts.

name.description: Unique name of this unit in PascalCase. Parts are prefixed with the name of the unit that contains them, e.g. `ButtonIcon` inside `Button`.

tokens.description: Token paths (dot separated, as in the token files) whose styles apply to this unit, e.g. `component.button.base`.

description.description: What this unit is for, in prose, for whoever meets it without the file: why it exists, what it is measured against, and the decisions a reader would otherwise have to reconstruct from the tokens. It is the text a design tool shows beside the component and the comment a generator can carry into code, so it is written for a human and never restates the keys around it.

placement.description: Where this unit is drawn inside whatever holds it, wherever it is placed. A slot's own `placement` overrides it. Omitted, the unit is in the flow.

content.description: What this unit renders. `text`: a run of text. `illustration`: a non-text visual such as an icon or a spinner. `image`: a picture the consumer supplies, such as a photo. `parts`: a container for other units, filled through `slots`. The bare word is shorthand for `{ "type": <word> }` and is the form to use whenever there is nothing else to say; `parts` always has slots and so has no shorthand.

text-content.description: A run of text the consumer supplies.

wrap.description: Whether the text breaks onto further lines when it does not fit. `false` keeps it on one line and ends it with an ellipsis.

maxLines.description: The most lines the text takes; the last one ends with an ellipsis. Omitted, the text takes as many lines as it needs. Only for text that wraps.

name.description: The component this unit draws, e.g. `Check` or `Spinner`; icons are components too. Omitted, the consumer picks what is drawn, and a preview shows a placeholder.

parts-content.description: A container for other units, filled through its slots.

placement.description: Where a unit is drawn. `flow`: one of the parts its holder's `layout` arranges, sized and spaced with its siblings. `overlay`: taken out of the flow and drawn over the holder's box, where it takes no space and no gap; `inline` and `block` say where on the box it sits, its offsets come from tokens. The bare word is shorthand for `{ "type": <word> }` and is the form to use whenever there is nothing else to say.

inline.description: Where the part sits along the holder's inline axis (left to right in a left-to-right script).

block.description: Where the part sits along the holder's block axis (top to bottom).

layout.description: How this unit arranges the parts in its slots. Only for units whose content is `parts`; omit it when there is nothing to arrange. Gaps come from tokens.

flow-layout.description: Places the parts in a single line along `direction`.

justify.description: Distribution of the parts along the main axis.

align.description: Alignment of the parts on the cross axis.

wrap.description: Whether the parts move onto a further line when they do not fit.

grid-layout.description: Places the parts in rows of equal columns, in slot order, starting a new row when one is full.

columns.description: How many columns of equal width each row has.

justify.description: Alignment of each part inside its cell along the row.

align.description: Alignment of each part inside its cell across the row.

slots.description: Named places where the consumer supplies a part. Keys are the slot names in camelCase. An optional slot gets a switch named `show<Slot>`.

required.description: Whether the consumer must fill this slot.

for.description: What fills this slot: the name of a unit in this file or of another component, or a list of them. The first entry is the default. `*` opens the slot to anything: alone, the slot has no default and a preview shows a placeholder; after a name (`["ButtonIcon", "*"]`), that unit is the default and anything may replace it.

placement.description: Where the part in this slot is drawn, overriding the part's own `placement`.

sizing.description: How the part in this slot is sized along its holder's `flow` direction. `hug`: as big as its content. `fill`: takes the space its siblings leave. Only for parts in the flow.

multiple.description: Whether the slot holds a list of parts instead of one, such as the tabs of a tab list. The parts are laid out by the holder's `layout`, in the order the consumer gives them.

state.description: Whose interaction states (hovered, pressed, focused, …) the part in this slot shows. `linked`: its holder's, so a card's title shows the card's hover. `own`: its own, because it takes input itself, like each tab of a tab list or a button inside a card; its own parts then link to it. A unit takes input when it is a component's first unit or sits in an `own` slot.

image-content.description: A picture the consumer supplies, such as a photo or a thumbnail. Unlike an illustration it is content, so it needs a text alternative from the consumer.

fit.description: How the picture fills the unit's box. `cover`: fills it and is cropped to it. `contain`: is shown whole, inside it.

overlay-alignment.description: `start`, `center` or `end` place the part at that side of the holder's box, at the size it takes. `stretch` spans the whole box: a bar along an edge is `stretch` on one axis and `end` on the other, a wash over the whole box is `stretch` on both.

variants.description: The axes this unit's tokens branch on, such as `size` or `emphasis`, with the values it has, in the order the axis defines them. Interaction states are not variants; they are listed in `states`. Omitted, the unit looks the same whatever its holder is set to.

states.description: The interaction states this unit's tokens style, such as `hovered` or `disabled`. They follow the user's interaction and are not picked like variants.

slot-config.description: The variants the part in this slot gets from its holder. A list is shorthand for `{ "inherit": <list> }`. Only variants are configured: interaction states (hovered, pressed, …) are not variants and always follow the part's own interaction. Omitted, the part gets nothing from its holder.

inherited-axes.description: Axes the part takes from its holder unchanged, by name: the holder's `size` sets the part's `size`. `*` passes every variant axis the two share. An axis that is also set to a value is not inherited.

config-value.description: The value one axis of the part gets. A value fixes it, whatever the holder shows. `from` and `map` translate one of the holder's axes: each holder value listed in `map` gives the part's value beside it, and a value not listed passes unchanged.

from.description: The holder's axis that is translated.

variant-value.description: One value of an axis: a name such as `md`, or `false`/`true` for an axis that is on or off, such as `destructive`.
